gallery.title: File:24-01-010-print.jpg
gallery.description:
During the First World War,
with anti-German sentiment running high,
hundreds of German "enemy aliens" were interned at
Fort Oglethorpe, Georgia.



This hand-colored wood-block print of the prison camp
appeared in the camp newsletter.

gallery.description:
Scope and content:  Original Caption: Preparing to move interned German sailors from Philadelphia to Georgia. Baggage of the interned sailors on the interned raiders at Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, being guarded by U.S. Marines. 1917. 700 interned sailors leave Philadelphia for internment at Fort Oglethorpe and McPherson, Georgia. March 26, 1917.
Date Taken: 1917
